summary: Partial continuation of PR #1657. Keeps the original 122 IDs, 14 ownership routes, 38 definition/construction API/test blocks and all 16 withheld items. Adds a characteristic-five positive-dimensional counterexample to unrestricted weighted Abel finiteness, an exact polynomial/principal-divisor certificate and a total-multiplicity rank refinement. Imports four verified generic library suppliers and one existing hyperelliptic model target; refines weighted-fibers to require nonzero total weights on overlap strata. Current totals: 131 items (9 library,20 planned,102 missing),86 missing routed once. Final version, characteristic-dependent geometry, microlocal constants, small-ratio dynamics and ramified torus dictionary remain open. No formalization is claimed.

items.name: Hyperelliptic double cover
items.statement: A smooth projective geometrically connected curve C of genus g≥2 equipped with a finite separable degree-two map π:C→P¹; κ=π*O(1) has degree two and τ is the deck involution. The routed geometric branch initially assumes char k≠2.
items.note: Model already planned upstream; scheme comparison and positive-characteristic extensions remain explicit inputs, not new AC layers. API: Import the AC.10 function-field model and the AC.12 curve dictionary; expose π, τ, κ, branch divisor, pullback and norm. Tests: (1) a genus-two curve over a perfect field supplies such a cover; (2) a purely inseparable degree-two map is excluded; (3) κ is a degree-two line bundle, not a chosen rational point.

items.name: Function-field Riemann–Roch space
items.statement: For a divisor D of an algebraic function field F/k, L(D) is the k-subspace of F of functions with div(f)+D≥0, including zero; ℓ(D)=finrank_k L(D), guarded by finite-dimensionality.
items.note: API: Reuse membership, monotonicity, principal-divisor transport and Divisor.dim; add the scheme H⁰ comparison through AC.12/JC.B. Tests: (1) zero lies in L(D); (2) a negative-degree divisor has no nonzero sections; (3) this carrier alone is not a coherent sheaf on a scheme.

items.name: Degree on function-field divisor classes
items.statement: For IsFunctionField k F, degreeClass:Cl(F)→Z descends the degree of divisors modulo principal divisors.
items.note: API: Reuse degreeClass, degreeClass_divisorClass and its kernel; supply the Picard-scheme comparison separately. Tests: (1) principal divisors map to zero; (2) degree is additive; (3) kernel finiteness does not supply a degree-one class.

items.name: Finite degree-zero function-field class group
items.statement: If F/k is an algebraic function field and k is finite, ker(degreeClass) is finite.
items.note: Read actual pinned theorem. It does not assert a rational point on C or representability of Pic⁰.

items.name: Finite projective-space cardinality
items.statement: For a finite-dimensional vector space V over F_q, (q−1)#P(V)=q^(dim V)−1, including V=0.
items.note: Pinned fraction-free formula uses Nat.card V−1. The vector-space cardinality substitution and scheme-fiber identification are separate.

items.name: Finite general-linear group cardinality
items.statement: For a finite field F_q, #GL_n(F_q)=∏_(0≤i<n)(q^n−q^i).

items.name: Picard degree components and Jacobian
items.statement: Pic^d(C) is the degree-d component of the relative Picard scheme, and J=Pic⁰(C). Over F_q, Pic^d(F_q) agrees with degree-d line-bundle classes only after the Brauer obstruction is removed.
items.note: API: Import sheafification, representability, degree components, translation, base change and tangent identification from JC; avoid silently identifying stack and scheme. Tests: (1) Pic⁰ is a scheme, not just a finite group; (2) a rational degree-one divisor need not be effective; (3) Picard functor points over general fields can have a descent obstruction.

items.name: Symmetric powers and Abel morphisms
items.statement: C^(d) represents effective degree-d divisors and is smooth projective of dimension d; A_d sends D to O_C(D).
items.note: API: Import relative effective divisors, base change, Abel maps and fiber linear systems from JC.C/D; expose universal divisor and addition. Tests: (1) C^(0) is a point; (2) C^(1)=C; (3) nonreduced divisors require tangent jets.

items.name: Coherent Riemann–Roch and duality on C
items.statement: For a line bundle L on a smooth projective geometrically connected curve, h⁰(L)−h¹(L)=deg L+1−g and H¹(L) is dual to H⁰(ω⊗L⁻¹).
items.note: This scheme statement is not marked built merely because the function-field theorem exists.

items.name: Bundles modulo line-bundle twists
items.statement: Bun₂(P¹) in this paper is the set of rank-two vector bundles on P¹_Fq modulo isomorphism and tensoring with a line bundle; equivalently PGL₂-bundle classes in the relevant trivial generic torsor class.
items.note: API: Construct the quotient, pushforward from a finite flat double cover and degree mod 2; import the actual Bun_G owner. Tests: (1) O⊕O and O(1)⊕O(1) agree; (2) O⊕O(1) has odd parity; (3) the GL₂ stack has infinitely many central-degree components.

items.name: Birkhoff–Grothendieck splitting
items.statement: Every rank-two vector bundle on P¹ over a field splits as O(a)⊕O(b), uniquely up to permuting a,b; modulo twisting its class is n=|a−b|.
items.note: Neither pinned library supplied this theorem; include its vector-bundle proof in GS.0, not just an abstract module splitting.

items.name: Automorphism orders of split bundles
items.statement: Over F_q, |Aut(O²)|=(q²−1)(q²−q); for n>0, |Aut(O⊕O(n))|=(q−1)²q^(n+1). Passing to PGL₂ divides both by q−1.
items.note: Use Hom(O(a),O(b))=H⁰(O(b−a)), triangularity when a≠b, and the built GL₂ cardinality.

items.name: Normalized inverse-automorphism bundle measure
items.statement: On N≃Bun₂(P¹), μ(0)=(q−1)/(2q), and μ(n)=(q²−1)/(2q^(n+1)) for n>0. Both parity components have mass 1/2.
items.note: API: Define probability mass function, sum weights, parity conditioning μ₀,μ₁ and tail events. Tests: (1) sum_n μ(n)=1; (2) μ(even)=μ(odd)=1/2; (3) unweighted counting on N cannot be normalized.

items.name: Bundle-measure parity tails
items.statement: For d≥1, μ(d+2N)=1/(2q^(d−1)); the d=0 case is 1/2 rather than q/2.

items.name: Finite Picard quotient and uniform law
items.statement: Q_C=Pic(C)/π*Pic(P¹)=Pic(C)/Zκ has two degree-parity fibers of cardinality h=#J(F_q), hence cardinality 2h, after the degree-one divisor-class and Brauer-descent inputs.
items.note: API: Construct quotient, translations, Haar/uniform measure and parity map; descend L↦π*L using the projection formula. Tests: (1) κ shifts degree by two; (2) translation by M preserves the uniform law; (3) absence of C(F_q) does not preclude a degree-one divisor class.

items.name: Degree-one divisor classes over finite fields
items.statement: A smooth projective geometrically connected curve over a finite field has index one: its closed-point degrees have gcd one, hence a divisor of degree one; this does not imply a rational point.
items.note: G3: original F.K. Schmidt/Lang proof still to acquire. The source claim that C has a rational point for large genus is not used.

items.name: Joint bundle pushforward
items.statement: For M,M′ on C, push uniform measure on Q_C along L↦(π*(L⊗M),π*(L⊗M′)). It depends on the ratio M⁻¹M′ up to the natural translations and has deterministic parity difference deg(M⁻¹M′) mod 2.
items.note: API: Construct pushforward, ratio invariance, marginals and fixed-parity subsequences. Tests: (1) M=M′ gives a diagonal law; (2) odd ratio forces opposite parities; (3) both marginals equal the one-bundle law.

items.name: Source one-bundle equidistribution
items.statement: For a fixed F_q and hyperelliptic curves with genera tending to infinity, the paper states convergence of the one-bundle pushforward to μ. Theorem 4.2 explicitly assumes q>4, while Theorem 1.1 omits this restriction.
items.note: G0/G3: retain the version discrepancy; the safe routed theorem below assumes q>4 and explicitly requires the analytic suppliers. This is not a claim for every q.

items.name: Source conditional joint equidistribution
items.statement: Assuming the uniform exponential Betti conjecture with base N, the paper states joint equidistribution for q>N⁴ when the minimum effective degree of the ratio modulo κ tends to infinity, after passage to a subsequence of fixed ratio parity.
items.note: G0/G7: record the source claim without accepting its undeveloped function-field Linnik transfer. The precise conditional assembly is routed separately.

items.name: Source bounded-ratio Hecke alternative
items.statement: If the minimum effective degree of the ratio fails to tend to infinity, the source asserts a subsequence represented by effective D_i with fixed pushforward D on P¹, and convergence of its joint measures to μ_D.
items.note: G7/G8: the subsequence extraction is elementary after bounded-degree finiteness, but the convergence and torus integral-model identification remain unclosed. Unrouted endpoint.

items.name: Effective divisor loci
items.statement: Θ_d⊂Pic^d(C) is the reduced image of A_d; Θ_d is empty for d<0 and is all Pic^d for d≥g. Comparing different degrees requires specified κ-translates or other line-bundle translations.
items.note: API: Expose inclusion, proper image, fibers, dimension and base change; keep translated degree components typed. Tests: (1) Θ₀ is the trivial class; (2) Θ_g=Pic^g; (3) Θ_(d−2) enters Pic^d via tensor κ.

items.name: Differential of the Abel map
items.statement: T_D C^(d)=H⁰(D,O_D(D)), T_L Pic^d=H¹(C,O_C); dA_D is the connecting map from 0→O_C→O_C(D)→O_D(D)→0, of rank d+1−h⁰(D).

items.name: Tangent image of a sum of Abel maps
items.statement: For effective D_i, the image of the differential of the sum map at (D_i) equals the Abel differential image for the divisor union max_i D_i.
items.note: Union takes maximum multiplicities, not the sum. The unweighted addition map is meant.

items.name: Weighted Abel differential with invertible multiplicities
items.statement: At distinct p_i with h⁰(O(Σp_i))=1, the differential of (p_i)↦O(Σd_i p_i) is injective when all d_i are nonzero in k.
items.note: G2: the v1 statement omits the invertibility hypothesis; multiplication by p has zero differential in characteristic p.

items.name: Unqualified weighted Abel claim
items.statement: V1 Proposition 2.3 asserts the weighted Abel differential has the unweighted injectivity property for arbitrary multiplicities, without a characteristic restriction.
items.note: G2: false in characteristic p with one multiplicity p. Corollary 2.4 cannot inherit this infinitesimal proof unchanged. The restricted version is the routed item. Continuation W4 strengthens the diagnosis: in characteristic 5 even the unrestricted finiteness conclusion has a positive-dimensional counterexample. Retain this source claim unrouted.

items.name: Weighted Abel quasi-finiteness near nonspecial reduced support
items.statement: On a fixed support/overlap stratum write the weighted divisor as Σ_j e_j p_j with distinct support points and total multiplicities e_j=Σ_i n_i m_ij. If h⁰(O(Σ_j p_j))=1 and every total e_j is nonzero in k, the differential is injective and the restricted weighted Abel map is locally quasi-finite there; each fixed-line-bundle fiber on that finite-type stratum is finite.
items.note: Do not infer the stated char-p claim from the unqualified Proposition 2.3. Continuation W1: nonzero original weights n_i alone are insufficient on overlaps (1+2=0 in characteristic 3). W4 proves unrestricted characteristic-p finiteness itself false using weights 5,1, not merely unproved by the printed differential argument.

items.name: Hyperelliptic and reduced parts of a divisor
items.statement: For effective D, write D=D_h+D_r where D_h is the maximal pullback divisor from P¹ and D_r contains no full hyperelliptic fiber. At a ramification point, D_h has even multiplicity 2 floor(mult/2).
items.note: API: Define h=deg(D_h)/2, residual divisor, involution, uniqueness, degree and linear-equivalence formulas. Tests: (1) p+τp reduces to κ; (2) a single ramification point stays in D_r; (3) three copies of a ramification point leave one residual copy.

items.name: Sections of the hyperelliptic pencil
items.statement: For 0≤h<g, pullback identifies H⁰(P¹,O(h)) with H⁰(C,hκ), of dimension h+1.

items.name: Canonical bundle of a hyperelliptic curve
Projective action of the involution
items.statement: The hyperelliptic involution acts trivially on P(H⁰(ω_C)).

items.name: Canonical map through the rational normal curve
items.statement: For g≥2 the canonical map factors through π followed by the degree-(g−1) Veronese P¹→P^(g−1).
items.note: G2: v1 writes O(g), inconsistent with the target dimension and ω=(g−1)κ; this item records the corrected degree.

items.name: Extended Gauss map of an Abel image
items.statement: For 1≤d≤g, the generic d-plane image of dA on C^(d) extends through Sym^d(P¹)=P^d by the length-d osculating span of the canonical rational normal curve.
items.note: API: Construct the Grassmannian-valued morphism, its factorization and agreement on h⁰(D)=1; include repeated-point jets. Tests: (1) d=1 gives the canonical map; (2) d=g is the constant full tangent space; (3) a double point uses an osculating plane.

items.name: Embedding by secant planes
items.statement: For d<g, the induced P^d→Gr(d,H¹(O_C)) is an embedding and the Gauss images agree exactly when π_*D agrees.

items.name: Independent canonical directions
items.statement: For k≤g points whose images on P¹ are pairwise distinct, their k canonical lines span a k-dimensional vector space, or projective dimension k−1.
items.note: Repeated π-images lower the dimension; jets require the separate osculating formulation.

items.name: Special divisor criterion
items.statement: For D=D_h+D_r with h=deg D_h/2 and r=deg D_r, h¹(D)>0 iff h+r≤g−1.

items.name: Complete linear system of a hyperelliptic divisor
items.statement: For D=D_h+D_r, if h=deg D_h/2 and r=deg D_r satisfy h+r≤g, then |D|=D_r+|hκ| and h⁰(D)=h+1.

items.name: Nash blowup
items.statement: For a reduced pure-dimensional variety X in a smooth ambient space, the Nash blowup is the closure of the graph of its tangent-space Gauss map over the smooth locus, with its map to X.
items.note: API: Construct tangent Grassmann bundle, graph closure, proper birational map and ambient-independence comparison. Tests: (1) a smooth X has identity Nash map; (2) the exceptional fibers retain limiting tangent spaces; (3) the blowup is not just the normalization.

items.name: Nash model of a proper theta locus
items.statement: For 1≤d<g, C^(d)→Θ_d is the Nash blowup, using the extended Gauss map and the residual-divisor description.
items.note: G2: d<g is required by the proof. For d=g and g≥2, Θ_g=J is smooth but the Abel map has positive-dimensional special fibers.

items.name: Unrestricted Nash statement in v1
items.statement: Proposition 2.15 prints C^(d) as the Nash blowup of Θ_d without a stated restriction on d.
items.note: G2: reject the literal all-d reading; d=g has smooth target and nontrivial Abel fibers, and d>g has positive relative dimension. Restricted item routed separately.

items.name: Sum maps from divisors and theta loci
items.statement: For 0≤a,b≤g define A_ab:C^(g−a)×C^(g−b)→Pic^(2g−a−b) and Σ_ab:Θ_(g−a)×Θ_(g−b)→Pic^(2g−a−b) by tensor product. A fiber of Σ is X_L=Θ_(g−a)∩(L−Θ_(g−b)).
items.note: API: Construct factorization through Abel maps, proper fibers and first-projection identification; retain expected dimension n=g−a−b. Tests: (1) a=b=0 gives X_L=J; (2) a=g gives a point or empty fiber; (3) a+b>g does not have a nonnegative expected dimension.

items.name: Rank formula at a pair of divisors
items.statement: Writing U=D₁∪D₂, rank dA_ab=min(g,deg(U_h)/2+deg(U_r)). A point is critical for the map exactly when this rank is below g.
items.note: Absolute singularity of a fiber also requires the expected-dimension hypothesis; record criticality without suppressing that distinction.

items.name: Canonical decomposition of two divisors
items.statement: Set Hcap=D₁h∩D₂h, H_i=D_ih−Hcap, S=D₁r∩(D₁r+D₂r)_h, Rcap=(D₁r−S)∩(D₂r−τS), R₁=D₁r−S−Rcap, R₂=D₂r−τS−Rcap. Then D₁=Hcap+H₁+S+Rcap+R₁ and D₂=Hcap+H₂+τS+Rcap+R₂.
items.note: API: Define min/max divisor operations, all seven effective pieces, reconstruction, disjointness and degree identities. Tests: (1) (p,τp) puts p in S and τp in the second divisor; (2) (p,p) contributes to Rcap; (3) a common full fiber contributes to Hcap.

items.name: Incorrect expanded septuple rank formula
items.statement: V1 Corollary 2.18 gives rank min(g,(deg Hcap+deg H₁+deg H₂)/2+deg S+deg Rcap+deg R₁+deg R₂).
items.note: G2: false for a ramification point p with D₁=p,D₂=2p and g≥2: H₂=2p,R₁=p, giving min(g,2), whereas D₁ union D₂=2p and the rank is 2+1−h⁰(2p)=1. Cross-overlap between a hyperelliptic part and the other residual part is not subtracted. The union-divisor formula is the routed target; all uses of this expanded formula require rechecking.

items.name: Effectivity index modulo the pencil
items.statement: For a line bundle L, e(L)=max{m∈Z:H⁰(C,L⊗κ^(−m))≠0}. It can be negative; e(L⊗κ^r)=e(L)+r.
items.note: API: Prove existence and boundedness using RR and degree; expose floor((deg L−g)/2)≤e(L)≤floor(deg L/2), shifts and Θ-membership. Tests: (1) e(O)=0; (2) e(κ^r)=r; (3) a noneffective line bundle can have negative e.

items.name: Incorrect lower bound in v1
items.statement: After Definition 2.19, v1 prints e(L)≥(2g−a−b−1)/2 for every L of degree 2g−a−b.
items.note: G2: false for generic L of degree g, for which e(L)=0, with g≥2 and a+b=g. RR gives only floor((deg L−g)/2) as a uniform lower bound. Unrouted.

items.name: Dimension and indexing of critical loci
items.statement: The canonical residual data give finitely many strata for the critical locus of A_ab^−1(L), each of dimension at most e(L); if e(L)≤n=g−a−b, the fiber has expected dimension n.
items.note: Route the characteristic-zero branch established using weighted differentials; all-characteristic transfer needs a separate proof, G2.

items.name: Middle perversity and intersection complexes
items.statement: For a finite-type scheme over a field and rational ℓ-adic coefficients with ℓ invertible, use the middle perverse heart and IC_X=j_!*(Q_ℓ[dim X]) for a pure-dimensional irreducible X.
items.note: API: Import truncation, recollement, intermediate extension, support/cosupport bounds and duality with its Tate twist. Tests: (1) Q_ℓ[d] is perverse on a smooth d-fold; (2) IC is not an unshifted constant sheaf; (3) integral coefficients do not inherit rational semisimplicity.

items.name: Geometric decomposition theorem
items.statement: For projective f and pure rational perverse K in the finite-field setting, Rf_*K decomposes after geometric base change into shifted perverse cohomology, each geometrically semisimple.
items.note: The splitting need not be canonical or preserve an arithmetic Weil structure; source-specific Frobenius comparisons require additional arguments.

items.name: Relative hard Lefschetz
items.statement: For projective f, pure rational perverse K and an f-ample class η, η^i:pH^(−i)(Rf_*K)→pH^i(Rf_*K)(i) is an isomorphism.

items.name: Semismall maps and relevant strata
items.statement: A proper map f:X→Y with X pure-dimensional is semismall when 2dim f⁻¹(y)≤dim X−dim S on each adapted stratum S; equality specifies relevant strata and their top-fiber local systems.
items.note: API: Define the dimension inequality independently of the decomposition theorem, stratified fiber local systems and induced summands. Tests: (1) C^(d)→Θ_d has P^r fibers on codimension-2r strata; (2) a positive-dimensional map to a point is generally not semismall; (3) a relevant local system need not be constant without proof.

items.name: Theta loci are rational homology manifolds
items.statement: For a hyperelliptic curve and 0≤d≤g, IC_(Θ_d)=Q_ℓ[d], using semismall Abel fibers and rank-one constant relevant local systems.
items.note: IY Proposition 2.8/Theorem 2.9 were read in the complex setting. An étale all-characteristic proof must re-establish this decomposition with Tate twists; it is not a literal transfer of complex singular cohomology.

items.name: Successive theta loci are set-theoretically ample sections
items.statement: After suitable translated identifications, Θ_d⊂Θ_(d+1) is set-theoretically the zero locus of an ample section; over F_q the construction is defined over every sufficiently large finite extension.
items.note: The proof uses non-Weierstrass points after extension. It does not provide such a point over F_q itself.

items.name: Low cohomology of theta loci
items.statement: For 0≤j<d≤g, restriction H^j(J_bar,Q_ℓ)→H^j((Θ_d)_bar,Q_ℓ) is an isomorphism, with the source-specific Frobenius compatibility.

items.name: High cohomology of theta loci
items.statement: For d<j and 0≤d≤g, H^j(Θ_d,Q_ℓ)≅H^(j+2g−2d)(J,Q_ℓ)(g−d).
items.note: Retain the Tate twist: geometric Frobenius on Q_ℓ(1) is q⁻¹.

items.name: Theta intersections as ample complete intersections set-theoretically
items.statement: If e(L)≤n=g−a−b≥0, X_L is pure of dimension n and, after sufficiently large finite extension, set-theoretically an intersection of a+b translates of Θ_(g−1) in J.
items.note: Set-theoretic lci is the assertion used; no scheme-theoretic regular-sequence claim is inferred.

items.name: Low cohomology of theta intersections
items.statement: If e(L)≤n=g−a−b, H^j(X_L,Q_ℓ)≅H^j(J,Q_ℓ) for 0≤j<n, compatibly with generalized Frobenius eigenspaces.

items.name: Semismallness away from a small locus
items.statement: The map (A×A)_L onto X_L is semismall outside a locus of dimension <e(L), with relevant loci Θ_(g−a−2r)∩(L−Θ_(g−b−2s)) and fibers P^r×P^s on the open strata.
items.note: Shifts by (r+s)κ must be included when typing the line-bundle degree on each lower locus.

items.name: Constant perverse sheaf to the intersection complex
items.statement: If e(L)≤n, Q_ℓ[n] on X_L is perverse and maps onto IC_(X_L), with a perverse kernel supported in dimension ≤e(L).
items.note: The surjectivity used in the displayed short exact sequence must be proved, not assumed from existence of a map.

items.name: High cohomology of theta intersections
items.statement: If 0≤a,b≤g, n=g−a−b≥0, and e(L)≤n, then for i>n+e(L), H^i(X_L,Q_ℓ)≅H^(i+2a+2b)(J,Q_ℓ)(a+b).
items.note: Precise internal theorem used instead of the introductory Θ_r shorthand. Dependence on the positive-characteristic geometry remains G2.

items.name: Exterior cohomology of a Jacobian
items.statement: For a g-dimensional Jacobian over an algebraically closed field and ℓ invertible, H*(J,Q_ℓ)=Λ*H¹(J,Q_ℓ), dim H¹=2g and total Betti number 4^g.
items.note: The existing abelian-variety carrier does not provide this cohomology theorem; exact realization supplier remains to locate.

items.name: Uniform theta-intersection Betti hypothesis
items.statement: The hyperelliptic hypothesis B(N) asserts a uniform exponential total-Betti bound N^g for X_L with fixed a,b, sufficiently large g, and e(L)≤g−a−b, over the relevant fields. The source also suggests removing the e(L) restriction.
items.note: API: State all quantifiers, ℓ≠char k, whether a,b are fixed, and whether N or an implicit constant is allowed; carry B(N) as a hypothesis. Tests: (1) a bound depending on C is insufficient; (2) an O_ε((960+ε)^g) bound does not give the exact base 960; (3) characteristic zero alone does not prove a finite-field hypothesis.

items.name: Source complex exponential Betti bound
items.statement: For C/C hyperelliptic and e(L)≤g−a−b, v1 Theorem 3.11 claims Σ_i dim H^i(X_L,Q)≪_ε(960+ε)^g.
items.note: G0/G4/G5: the numerical base is withheld because the printed polar calculation and signed Morse inequality require repair. Record the ε-dependent statement exactly; not ≤960^g.

items.name: Only the middle perverse direct image is nonconstant
items.statement: For Σ_ab, the low-cohomology comparison identifies negative perverse direct images of Q_ℓ[2g−a−b] with shifted constant cohomology of J; relative hard Lefschetz controls positive indices. Stalk bounds reduce to pH⁰(RΣ_*Q_ℓ[2g−a−b]) plus an explicitly bounded constant contribution.
items.note: Specify shifts and twists in the future proof; there is no unshifted equality of all perverse images.

items.name: Alternative high-cohomology range in characteristic zero
items.statement: For C/C and e(L)≤g−a−b, the source obtains H^i(X_L,Q)≅H^(i+2a+2b)(J,Q)(a+b) for i>g−(a+b)/2+e(L), using higher-discriminant support.
items.note: This range is weaker than Theorem 3.9 and does not use its exact same proof.

items.name: Chow operations and Chern classes
items.statement: Use Chow groups with proper pushforward, flat and refined lci pullback, Chern classes and intersection products, with explicit cycle multiplicities and rational coefficients where required.
items.note: API: Import projection and excess-intersection formulas, top-Chern Euler characteristic and degree pairing. Tests: (1) [2]_* on a u-dimensional abelian cycle scales its cohomology class by 4^u; (2) image and pushforward cycles can differ by generic degree; (3) excess components require refined intersection.

items.name: Chern class of a symmetric power
items.statement: In the rational cohomology ring of C^(g−a), c(TC^(g−a))=(1+x)^(1−a) exp(−θ/(1+x)), where x is the point-addition divisor class and θ is pulled back from J.
items.note: Acquire the original ring presentation, truncation and sign normalization before the coefficient computation, G9.

items.name: Poincaré class of a theta locus
items.statement: For 0≤d≤g, [Θ_d]=θ^(g−d)/(g−d)! in rational cohomology of J, with ∫_J θ^g=g!.

items.name: Euler number of a smooth general Abel-sum fiber
items.statement: In characteristic zero, for 0≤a,b≤g and a+b≤g, a smooth expected-dimensional general fiber F of A_ab satisfies |χ(F)|≤8^g.
items.note: Proof uses the actual symmetric-power Chern formula, Poincaré formula and binomial cancellation; original suppliers are still acquisition gaps.

items.name: Local Euler obstruction
items.statement: For an irreducible complex subvariety V of a smooth Y, Eu_V is its constructible local Euler obstruction, extended by zero, equal to one on V_smooth.
items.note: API: Construct from the Nash bundle, prove stratified constructibility and that Eu_V form the integral triangular basis of constructible functions. Tests: (1) Eu_Y=1 for smooth Y; (2) support is V; (3) χ(Q_Y[dim Y])=(−1)^dim Y, so its coefficient can be negative.

items.name: Polar varieties and multiplicities
items.statement: For a pure-dimensional complex germ V⊂Y, a generic linear projection determines polar varieties; γ_i(V,x) is the local multiplicity of the i-dimensional polar cycle, with the top-dimensional convention explicit.
items.note: API: Construct conormal incidence, generic-choice independence and local cycle multiplicity; compare with vanishing-cycle definitions. Tests: (1) a smooth d-fold has γ_d=1; (2) genericity excludes the discriminant arrangement; (3) a set-theoretic image loses possible cycle multiplicities.

items.name: Incorrect signed Morse inequality as printed
items.statement: V1 Theorem 3.12 writes χ(K)=Σn_α Eu_(Vα) and dim H^(−i)(K)_x≤Σn_α γ_i(Vα,x) for a perverse K.
items.note: G4: K=Q_C[1] on a smooth complex curve has χ=−1 and γ₁=1, giving the false bound 1≤−1. Use effective characteristic-cycle coefficients with the correct dimension signs or a valid absolute-value bound; original Massey statement remains to acquire.

items.name: Characteristic cycle with normalized signs
items.statement: For a constructible complex K on a smooth complex variety, normalize CC so that perverse sheaves have effective cycles and CC(Q_Y[dim Y]) is the zero section with multiplicity one.
items.note: API: Construct CC, local index formula and its relation to Eu_V including (−1)^dim V; use CC coefficients in stalk bounds. Tests: (1) shift by one negates CC; (2) Q_C[1] has positive zero-section coefficient; (3) naive Euler pushforward is not functorial for wild Artin–Schreier covers.

items.name: Characteristic-cycle polar bound
items.statement: For a perverse sheaf K on a smooth complex variety, dim H^(−i)(K)_x is bounded by the ith polar multiplicity of its effective characteristic cycle, with the matching cycle convention.
items.locator: Massey input to Theorem 3.12; Sawin Theorem 1.4 comparison
items.note: This is a source-acquisition target, not a proof supplied by the false printed n_α formula. Sawin gives an independent characteristic-p formulation for perfect k and ℓ invertible.

items.name: Higher discriminants
items.statement: For a proper map f:X→Y of smooth complex varieties, Δ^i(f) consists of y admitting no (i−1)-dimensional tangent subspace transverse to f along the entire fiber.
items.note: API: Construct closed loci, transversality along fibers, codimension estimates and relation to singular support. Tests: (1) Δ¹ is the critical-value locus; (2) a smooth map has empty positive discriminants; (3) inseparable maps in characteristic p invalidate automatic codim Δ^i≥i.

items.name: Codimension of higher discriminants
items.statement: For proper maps between smooth complex varieties, codim Δ^i(f)≥i; supports of the relevant direct-image constituents lie among the closures of codimension-i components.
items.note: Published MS §3 explicitly requires a separate codimension hypothesis in positive characteristic; no blanket transfer is routed.

items.name: Euler-obstruction expansion by higher discriminants
items.statement: For proper smooth-source f over C, χ(Rf_*Q_X) is an integral sum of Eu_(Δ^(i,α)); coefficients are generic transverse-slice vanishing-cycle Euler values with fixed Φ convention.
items.note: MS supplies signed characteristic-cycle conversion (−1)^codim in its convention. Do not substitute these possibly signed coefficients directly into a dimension bound.

items.name: Motivic Abel-fiber decomposition and inversion
items.statement: After typing κ shifts, [A_ab]=Σ_(r,s≥0) L^(r+s)[Σ_(a+2r,b+2s)] in the relative Grothendieck group. Thus [Σ_ab]=[A_ab]−L[A_(a+2,b)]−L[A_(a,b+2)]+L²[A_(a+2,b+2)].
items.note: G4: v1 has inconsistent indices and a missing L in one inverse term. Euler specialization L↦1 gives the four-term constructible-function identity; this is not an equality of derived objects without shifts and twists.

items.name: Transverse slices along a canonical residual stratum
items.statement: In characteristic zero, for the locus with Rcap fixed and R₁+R₂ fixed, put r=deg(R₁+R₂+Rcap). A generic (g−r)-plane is transverse to A_ab along that locus, and no smaller-dimensional plane is.

items.name: Candidate higher-discriminant varieties
items.statement: V_(r,s)=Θ_r+[2](Θ_s), with translations identifying degree components and r,s≥0, r+s≤g−1. Here [2](X) is an image, while [2]⁻¹(X) denotes the full inverse image.
items.note: API: Construct the addition image, dimension, generic presentation and conormal incidence; distinguish image cycle from pushforward cycle. Tests: (1) V_(r,0)=Θ_r; (2) V_(0,1) is the doubled curve; (3) [2]⁻¹(X) includes all two-torsion translates.

items.name: Higher-discriminant component containment
items.statement: In characteristic zero, codimension-i components of Δ^i(A_ab) occur among translated V_(r,s) with r+s=g−i.
items.note: Containment among candidates does not assert every V_(r,s) occurs or has multiplicity one.

items.name: Ordinary quadratic singularity and vanishing module
items.statement: An ordinary quadratic hypersurface singularity is defined through its completed or étale local equation and smooth projective tangent quadric; its vanishing cycles have the source-qualified rank-one middle-degree description.
items.note: API: Import LPV local model, Milnor/vanishing module, orientation and twist; specialize the complex nondegenerate-Hessian branch. Tests: (1) a node has one vanishing cycle; (2) a degenerate Hessian is excluded; (3) characteristic two needs a separate polar-form convention.

items.name: Nodal slices of Abel-sum maps
items.statement: At a generic point of V_(r,s), the source-specific transverse sliced Abel-sum map has only ordinary double points, at most 10^g.
items.note: Complex analytic Hessian proof; slice dimensions and generic unramified support must be retained. It is not an all-characteristic theorem.

items.name: Incidence model for polar cycles of V_(r,s)
items.statement: For r+s≤g−1, use C^r_sym×C^s_sym×P^(g−1−r−s), mapping to J by D+[2]E and to P^(g−1) by the sum π_*D+π_*E+F. Polar loci arise from inverse images of annihilator linear spaces.
items.note: API: Define both proper maps, exceptional discriminant B and pushforward cycle with generic degree. Tests: (1) r=s=0 reduces to the auxiliary projective factor; (2) an annihilator reverses linear-space dimension; (3) ramification hyperplanes are part of B.

items.name: Generic incidence realization of the polar locus
items.statement: For an annihilator linear space avoiding containment in B, the auxiliary incidence image contains the polar locus; for a general choice equality holds in the source setting.
items.note: G5: statement prints L⊂B while its proof uses L∨ not contained in B. The routed statement uses the latter, with exact scheme/cycle comparison still to prove.

items.name: Disputed polar-cycle coefficient
items.statement: V1 Lemma 3.22 computes its coefficient using [2]_*[Θ_u]=2^u[Θ_u] and concludes a g²24^g upper bound.
items.note: G5: in cohomology [2]_* on a u-dimensional abelian cycle scales by 2^(2u)=4^u. For r=0,s=1,k=g−2 the displayed coefficient is 2, while the pushforward doubled-curve cycle has coefficient 4. Generic image degree must also be checked. Unrouted numerical display.

items.name: Disputed exponential polar-multiplicity bound
items.statement: V1 Proposition 3.23 claims mult_x P_L(V_(r,s))≤g²96^g.
items.note: G5: depends on the disputed preceding coefficient; the lift of a normalization to a proper surjective product also needs a finite base change. Keep qualitative construction but withhold the numerical bound.

items.name: Nonnegative intersection contributions on an abelian variety
items.statement: For proper intersections in an abelian variety, the refined contribution of each connected component is nonnegative under the cited nef-tangent intersection theorem; an isolated-point contribution bounds local multiplicity in the stated setting.
items.note: G9: acquire the exact Fulton hypotheses and multiplicity theorem; trivial tangent bundle supplies nefness, not a license to ignore excess-intersection data.

items.name: Splitting index from sections
items.statement: For L∈Pic^(g−1), the bundle index of π*L is 2h⁰(L); for L∈Pic^(g−2), it is 2h⁰(L)+1.
items.note: RR gives Euler characteristics 0 and −1 respectively; compute h⁰ of the split bundle on P¹, including the zero-section cases.

items.name: Divisors with no hyperelliptic pair
items.statement: C₀^(n) is the locus of effective degree-n divisors containing no full π-fiber. For n≤g, each effective line-bundle class is uniquely represented by a reduced divisor followed by a κ-power.
items.note: API: Construct reduced locus, unique residual representative in the nonspecial range and the Θ_n disjoint stratification by C₀^(n−2j). Tests: (1) p+τp is excluded; (2) a single branch point is allowed; (3) degree beyond g requires extra linear-system analysis.

items.name: Curve zeta series and numerator
items.statement: For smooth projective geometrically connected C/F_q, Z_C(t)=Σ_n #C^(n)(F_q)t^n=P_C(t)/((1−t)(1−qt)), with P_C(0)=1 and degree 2g.
items.note: API: Import the closed-point Euler product, effective-divisor coefficient identity, rationality and finite-extension normalization. Tests: (1) P¹ has numerator 1; (2) closed points of degree two contribute to C^(2)(F_q); (3) F_q-points of the symmetric power are not merely multisets of C(F_q).

items.name: Curve numerator functional equation
items.statement: P_C(t)=(qt²)^g P_C(1/(qt)).
items.note: Geometric Frobenius and reversed characteristic polynomial conventions are fixed by WC.2.

items.name: Jacobian point count from the curve numerator
items.statement: #J(F_q)=P_C(1)=q^g P_C(q⁻¹) for smooth projective geometrically connected C/F_q.
items.note: Requires the actual curve/Jacobian realization comparison, not merely numerator reciprocity.

items.name: Curve Riemann hypothesis and extension counts
items.statement: Every root of P_C has absolute value q^(−1/2), in every complex embedding, and |#C(F_(q^r))−(q^r+1)|≤2g q^(r/2).
items.note: WC.5 consumes the RH supplier; no pinned general-genus implementation was found.

items.name: Generating series for reduced effective divisors
items.statement: Σ_n #C₀^(n)(F_q)t^n=(1−t²)(1−qt²)Z_C(t), using unique removal of full π-fibers.

items.name: Point counts from a finite morphism to P¹
items.statement: If π:C→P¹ over F_q is finite of degree r, then #C(F_(q^m))≤r(q^m+1) for every m≥1.
items.note: The morphism must be defined over the ground field; geometric gonality alone does not give this rational-point inequality.

items.name: Weil-angle measure and Lindelöf family
items.statement: For genus g>0, the normalized multiset of reciprocal roots divided by √q defines a probability measure on the unit circle. A fixed-q family is Lindelöf when max_|t|=q^−1/2 |P_C(t)|=O_ε(q^(εg)) for every ε>0.
items.note: API: Construct empirical measures with multiplicity, weak convergence, logarithmic potentials and uniform maxima; distinguish genus and q limits. Tests: (1) repeated eigenangles retain their multiplicity; (2) RH alone allows exponential maxima; (3) the universal curve family is not automatically Lindelöf.

items.name: Sublinear gonality implies Lindelöf
items.statement: For a fixed finite field and a family with ground-field gonality o(g), normalized Weil measures tend to Haar and the family satisfies the above critical-circle Lindelöf upper bound. In particular this applies to hyperelliptic curves.
items.note: AT writes F_p; its §3 proof only uses fixed-field extension counts and Weil RH. The extension from the paper notation to prime powers is explicit proof work; its general metaplectic restrictions are not silently imported.

items.name: Subexponential normalization of the Jacobian count
items.statement: For a fixed-q hyperelliptic family with g→∞, #J(F_q)=q^(g+o(g)); equivalently log P_C(q⁻¹)=o(g).
items.note: Derived supplier: Haar convergence of Weil angles integrates the continuous function log|1−q^−1/2 z|, since q>1. This gives BOTH bounds and avoids dividing by a one-sided critical-circle bound.

items.name: Reduced-divisor coefficient estimate
items.statement: For fixed q>1 and every ε>0, coefficient extraction gives #C₀^(n)(F_q)=q^(n−g)(1−q⁻²)#J(F_q)+O_(q,ε)(q^(n/2+εg)), uniformly in n≥0 along the Lindelöf family.
items.note: G3: the printed exponent (n/2+ε)g is a typo; the contour factor is q^(n/2), and the εg factor comes only from the numerator bound. Use the pole residue at q⁻¹ and a circle free of denominator poles.

items.name: Asymptotic proportion of effective classes
items.statement: For each fixed integer a≥0, a fixed-q hyperelliptic family satisfying the Lindelöf and class-normalization suppliers has #Θ_(g−a)(F_q)/#J(F_q)→q^(−a).
items.note: Sum the reduced coefficients for n=g−a−2j; the geometric factor 1−q⁻² cancels. Uniform error summation and the terminal tail must be proved.

items.name: One-bundle equidistribution with explicit inputs
items.statement: For fixed q>4, genus tending to infinity, and the curve/Picard dictionary and analytic suppliers above, the uniform Q_C pushforward converges weakly on N to the inverse-automorphism probability μ.
items.note: Tails determine point masses, and their geometric decay gives tightness. No unproved rational-point existence or all-q endpoint is assumed.

items.name: Exponential total Betti bound for theta loci
items.statement: For 0≤d≤g, the source obtains Σ_i dim H^i(Θ_d,Q_ℓ)=O(4^g), via semismall Abel decomposition and symmetric-power cohomology.
items.note: Macdonald and étale comparison suppliers require G9. This is the single-theta bound, not the intersection conjecture.

items.name: Weights for the compact-support counting error
items.statement: For X/F_q separated of finite type, constant rational ℓ-adic coefficients have H_c^i weights ≤i; if X is proper this applies to H^i, including singular X.

items.name: Finite-field trace formula
items.statement: For separated finite-type X/F_q and ℓ∤q, #X(F_q)=Σ_i(−1)^i Tr(Frob_q|H_c^i(X_bar,Q_ℓ)), with geometric Frobenius and Tate twists consistently normalized.
items.note: G9: generic trace-formula owner is upstream CohomologicalPointCounting/PR196; exact supplier stage and original statement remain to read. Unrouted until checked, rather than assigning this theorem to the weights stage.

items.name: Threshold for the geometric one-bundle proof
items.statement: Using a total Betti bound O(4^g), high-cohomology comparison and #J=q^(g+o(g)), the elementary error is O(4^g q^(−g/2+o(g))), which tends to zero when q>16.
items.note: This proof alone does not justify its theorem heading q>4. The analytic proof is a separate supplier.

items.name: Effective-degree escape modulo κ
items.statement: For [M]∈Q_C let m([M]) be the minimum n≥0 admitting an effective degree-n representative after a κ-shift. Escape means m([M_i])→∞.
items.note: API: Prove well-definedness, existence from RR, invariance under κ, parity and bounded-degree subsequence extraction. Tests: (1) [O] has m=0; (2) a fixed effective representative prevents escape; (3) unbounded degrees of chosen M_i do not imply escape.

items.name: Correct joint tail normalization
items.statement: For compatible degree parities, a joint tail event corresponding to X_L has probability #X_L(F_q)/(2#J(F_q)) under the uniform law on Q_C; incompatible parities give probability zero.
items.note: G3: v1 prints equality with the raw cardinality. The factor 2h is mandatory; conditional-on-parity probabilities instead have denominator h.

items.name: Error estimate in the large-effectivity-distance case
items.statement: Assuming B(N), high-cohomology comparison and #J=q^(g+o(g)), if L∉Θ_(εg) for a fixed 0<ε<1, the normalized low-degree counting error is bounded by N^g q^(−εg/4+o(g)), up to fixed a,b constants.
items.note: It tends to zero if q>N^(4/ε). For q>N⁴ choose ε<1 sufficiently close to 1; do not interchange the quantifiers.

items.name: Parity-conditioned product law
items.statement: Write μ₀=2μ restricted to even n and μ₁=2μ restricted to odd n. For ratio parity δ∈{0,1}, the predicted law is 1/2(μ₀⊗μ_δ+μ₁⊗μ_(1+δ mod 2)).
items.note: API: Construct the product mixture and prove its marginals, total mass and parity support. Tests: (1) δ=0 gives equal parities; (2) δ=1 includes BOTH even×odd and odd×even; (3) plain μ⊗μ assigns mass to forbidden parities.

items.name: Joint limit conditional on both proof branches
items.statement: For fixed q>N⁴, a genus-growing hyperelliptic sequence with escaping ratios and fixed parity δ has joint law tending to the parity-conditioned product, PROVIDED B(N), the high-cohomology and trace suppliers, class normalization, and the required function-field small-ratio Linnik theorem all hold.
items.note: This routes the exact implication, not an unconditional theorem. G7 is a named unclosed hypothesis; Sawin supplies a later Betti claim but does not by itself replace the missing local integral-model verification.

items.name: Small split place for a hyperelliptic double cover
items.statement: The proof requires an unramified split closed point of P¹ whose degree is O(log_q g), uniformly in the cover; obtain it from curve point counts with explicit treatment of lower-degree points and ramification.
items.note: The literal 2 log g needs base and additive constants; route only O(log_q g) until the effective inequality is proved.

items.name: Unproved transfer in the small-ratio case
items.statement: The source says the proof of the number-field EMiV §10.3 corollary carries over to function fields using a split place of degree ≤2 log g, yielding mixing for ratios of effective degree ≤εg.
items.note: G7: acquire and rederive the positive-characteristic dynamics, entropy/recurrence and variable-place uniformity. A statement that a proof carries over is not a closed supplier. The optional Waldspurger sketch explicitly says the available AT formula is not general enough.

items.name: Adelic group and integral model
items.statement: For k=F_q(P¹), G(A_k) is the restricted product of G(k_v) relative to a chosen smooth integral model at almost all v; quotients retain the diagonal G(k).
items.note: API: Import topology, restricted Haar measures, quotient measure, change of model and restriction of scalars. Tests: (1) GL₁ gives ideles; (2) a ramified place is not automatically hyperspecial; (3) changing finitely many compact opens changes the level.

items.name: Adelic construction of a vector bundle
items.statement: For g∈GL_r(A_k), glue the O_v-lattices g_v O_v^r inside the generic k^r to a vector bundle; left GL_r(k) changes the generic frame and right ∏GL_r(O_v) changes integral frames.
items.note: API: Construct local lattices, gluing, inverse generic framing, and the groupoid/double-coset dictionary with automorphism groups. Tests: (1) r=1 recovers divisor classes; (2) generic triviality is a hypothesis for general G; (3) a frame change does not change the underlying bundle.

items.name: Weil double-coset classification
items.statement: For GL_r over a smooth projective curve, GL_r(k) ∖ GL_r(A)/∏GL_r(O_v) classifies vector bundles; for a general G the corresponding quotient describes the generically trivial torsor class, with other generic classes treated separately.

items.name: Torus associated with a separable quadratic extension
items.statement: For a separable quadratic extension l/k, T=Res_(l/k) G_m/G_m embeds in PGL₂ by the multiplication representation after a k-basis of l; T(k)=l×/k× by Hilbert 90.
items.note: API: Construct the quotient torus, basis-change conjugacy, local points, unit integral model and central quotient. Tests: (1) split l gives a split torus; (2) a ramified field extension is anisotropic locally; (3) T has a PGL₂ representation, not a canonical GL₂ lift.

items.name: Ramified maximal-compact error in the appendix
items.statement: The appendix identifies T(O_v) with the maximal compact and asserts it can be conjugated into PGL₂(O_v) for the quadratic-torus embedding.
items.note: G8: for l_v=k_v(√π), the compact anisotropic group l_v×/k_v× contains √π, represented by [[0,π],[1,0]]. Its determinant valuation is odd, invariant under conjugacy and scalar multiplication modulo 2, so it cannot lie in PGL₂(O_v). The unit quotient has index two and is not the maximal compact. Unrouted literal statement.

items.name: Unit-level torus dictionary
items.statement: Use the image of O_(l_v)× in l_v×/k_v× as the level subgroup, including at ramified places. An integral O_(l_v)-lattice basis gives the pushforward bundle from a line bundle on C, after quotienting by base line-bundle twists.
items.note: G8: corrected target; comparison to the source measure and exact adelic quotient still requires proof. Do not claim a map T→GL₂ from the multiplication representation. API: Construct local integral bases, lattice multiplication and the Res G_m→GL₂ map before passing to T→PGL₂; prove compatibility with π_* and central quotients. Tests: (1) ramified uniformizer is outside the unit-level subgroup; (2) unramified extension has valuation quotient zero; (3) a base line-bundle twist becomes scalar and disappears in PGL₂.

items.name: Hecke correspondence of an effective base divisor
items.statement: For effective D=Σn_v[v] on P¹, use local diag(1,π_v^n_v) and K₀(D) to define a correspondence of bundle classes. Equivalently choose W⊂V with quotient O_D, modulo common line-bundle twist.
items.note: API: Construct double-coset correspondence, lattice modifications, finite fibers and local primitive flags; import the global Hecke owner. Tests: (1) D=0 gives the diagonal; (2) degree-one D gives q_v+1 local choices; (3) a nonprimitive vector modulo π^n does not define a direct-summand flag.

items.name: Hecke measure with automorphism weights
items.statement: μ_D is the pushforward of normalized invariant measure on the adelic PGL₂ quotient along x↦(xK,xg_DK), or the equivalent weighted measure on modifications.
items.note: API: Define using quotient measure, verify finite volume, marginals and independence of uniformizers; keep stabilizer weights. Tests: (1) μ₀ is diagonal; (2) both marginals are μ; (3) parity difference equals deg D mod 2.

items.name: Hecke equidistribution input
items.statement: The appendix uses the Ramanujan/spectral estimate to make μ_D approach the parity-conditioned product as deg D→∞ along fixed degree parity.
items.note: G7: exact spectral normalization and function-field Ramanujan supplier not extracted. Do not assert convergence to μ⊗μ across both parity components. Unrouted until the theorem is read.

items.name: Later characteristic-p theorem to acquire fully
items.statement: Sawin arXiv:1907.04850v2 Theorems 1.4 and 1.6 claim a characteristic-p perverse-stalk bound and, for char k≠2, total Betti bound 28^g/16+4·8^g+2·4^g for all 0≤a,b≤g and all L. Theorem 1.7 states a mixing consequence for q>28⁴.
items.note: G6: selected introduction, polar coefficient discussion and Appendix A read, not the complete proof. The coefficient quoted from ST Lemma 3.22 repeats the 2-power requiring reconciliation. Its odd-parity display repeats even×odd twice; the correct mixture has both cross terms. Leave the numeric endpoint unrouted until original final versions and cycle conventions are checked.

items.name: Characteristic-power binomial identities
items.statement: In a commutative ring of prime characteristic p, (x+y)^(p^n)=x^(p^n)+y^(p^n) and (x−y)^(p^n)=x^(p^n)−y^(p^n).
items.note: Statements, standing hypotheses and supporting proofs read. These algebra identities do not construct a curve or identify a Jacobian Frobenius with scalar multiplication.

items.name: Linear equivalence from an explicit principal divisor
items.statement: For an order system S and divisors D,E, S.LinearlyEquivalent D E iff there exists g with S.principalDivisor g=D−E.
items.note: Read the actual OrderSystem, principalDivisor and witness equivalence. The concrete point orders must be supplied; a polynomial identity alone is not a divisor computation.

items.name: Formal Abel–Jacobi class sums
items.statement: For an order system with degree-zero principal divisors and a weight-one base point, the degree-corrected Abel–Jacobi divisor class is additive, respects integral multiples, and its equality for equal-degree divisors is equivalent to linear equivalence.
items.note: Actual statements/proofs read. This is the existing formal divisor-class shadow; it is not the Abel morphism of schemes or its differential. Reuse it after the concrete order-system comparison.

items.name: Linearly equivalent divisors have isomorphic sheaves
items.statement: On a Noetherian integral scheme with DVR stalks at codimension-one points, linearly equivalent Weil divisors D,E have isomorphic divisor sheaves O(D),O(E), via multiplication by their witnessing rational function.
items.note: Actual theorem and multiplication-isomorphism proof read, including ambient hypotheses. The geometric model and its point-to-divisor adapter remain explicit, not already implemented by this import.

items.name: Characteristic-five genus-two model instance
items.statement: Over an algebraically closed field k of characteristic 5, the smooth projective model of y²=x⁵−x has genus 2, one point ∞ above infinity, ord_∞ x=−2 and ord_∞ y=−5, and involution τ(x,y)=(x,−y).
items.locator: Algebraic Curves Layer 10 odd-degree hyperelliptic model and Layer 12 dictionary; continuation W2
items.note: This is an instance of existing upstream model/comparison plans, not a new hyperelliptic carrier. Two smooth affine charts and the six tame branch points give the mathematical check; generic Riemann–Hurwitz remains with upstream Layer 7.

items.name: Exact weighted Abel rank on distinct nonspecial support
items.statement: For distinct p₁,…,p_r on a smooth curve over an algebraically closed field, with h⁰(O(Σp_j))=1, the differential of (p_j)↦O(Σe_jp_j) has rank #{j:e_j≠0 in k} and kernel the direct sum of the tangent lines whose e_j vanish in k. On a fixed overlap stratum first combine e_j=Σ_i n_i m_ij.
items.locator: Proposition 2.3, corrected characteristic-sensitive refinement; continuation W1
items.note: Independent tangent lines follow from abel-tangent on the reduced divisor. Multiplication by e_j scales each line. This strengthens weighted-abel without duplicating the underlying Abel morphism.

items.name: Polynomial certificate for the characteristic-five fiber
items.statement: In characteristic 5 set H_b(t)=b⁶+2b⁴t+3b²t²+4t³ and U=b¹⁰+b². Then b¹⁰(b²+t⁵−t)−H_b(t)²=t⁵(U−t) and H_b(U)=−b³⁰. If b²=a⁵−a, then U=a²⁵−a.
items.locator: Continuation W2–W3, explicit counterexample to the unrestricted reading of v1 Corollary 2.4
items.note: An exact coefficient identity over F₅[b,t], not a numerical conjecture. It avoids any unproved identification of Jacobian Frobenius with [5]. Verified symbolically and in F₁₂₅.

items.name: Explicit principal divisor in characteristic five
items.statement: On the model above let P=(a,b), b≠0 and a²⁵≠a, Q=(a²⁵,−b²⁵), t=x−a, G_P=b⁵y−H_b(t). Then div(G_P)=5P+Q−6∞, so O(5P+Q)≅O(6∞).
items.locator: Continuation W3: local orders at P,Q,∞
items.note: The norm certificate gives exact orders 5 and 1 because the conjugate factor is a unit at both points. The cubic term gives the unique pole of order 6 at infinity; no other zeros occur. The geometric order adapter must still be implemented on the existing model.

items.name: Positive-dimensional weighted Abel fiber with nonspecial support
items.statement: For C:y²=x⁵−x over an algebraically closed field of characteristic 5, the nonempty open set U={P=(a,b):b≠0,a²⁵≠a} maps into one fiber of (P,Q)↦O(5P+Q), via P↦(P,τ(P²⁵)). The support P+Q has h⁰=1, yet the divisors 5P+Q in |6∞| are infinitely many and form a one-dimensional family.
items.locator: Continuation W4; v1 p.7 Corollary 2.4 under an unrestricted characteristic reading
items.note: Q has different x-coordinate from P, so P+Q contains no hyperelliptic fiber and Lemma 2.13 gives h⁰=1. The coefficient-5 point recovers P, proving nonconstancy. This is stronger than a zero differential. It does not refute characteristic-zero finiteness or by itself any later finite-field equidistribution theorem.
